title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Hazardous-Cargo Surcharge at Loading
content:
## What this governs

When the goods of a Dangerous Goods Acceptance file are loaded, the line raises one hazardous-cargo surcharge on that acceptance. The desk books it as a single surcharge entry on the acceptance's dangerous-goods account; afterwards the account shows the entry, dated on the day of booking, and a correspondingly higher balance.

## Booking tool: `book_dg_loading_surcharge_44d311b2`

**What the tool proves it does.** Each call writes one surcharge charge to the acceptance's dangerous-goods account, records the number of containers it was computed on, and adds the amount to what the acceptance owes. An identical repeated call writes nothing further and leaves the balance as it was.

**Access.** The tool is not on the desk's open list. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and, once unlocked, calls it on its own side of the conversation.

**Parameters, one by one.**

- `dg_id` — identifier of the dangerous-goods acceptance whose goods were loaded, as the acceptance lookup reports it.
- `charge_code` — tariff code of the entry; the only value accepted is `dg_surcharge`. Neither the marine-pollutant charge nor any other dangerous-goods charge can be booked through this tool.
- `container_count` — the number of containers the surcharge is computed on; a whole number of containers.
- `amount_usd` — the surcharge to book, a US-dollar amount held to the cent (half cents rounded up) when it is passed.

**Receipt on success.** `dg_event_id` for the new charge, `dg_id`, `charge_code` (always `dg_surcharge`), `container_count` as charged, `amount_usd` as booked to 2 decimals, and `charges_due_usd`, what the acceptance owes in dangerous-goods charges with the entry included.

| Field in the receipt | Content |
|---|---|
| `dg_event_id` | reference of the new charge |
| `charge_code` | `dg_surcharge` |
| `charges_due_usd` | outstanding balance after booking, 2 decimals |
